fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime conspicuity of a HAWK/PHB display against background clutter is a substantive safety issue at a pedestrian arterial crossing in final design, with a clear mechanism (late/missed stop decision endangering crossing pedestrians).
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (drivers confused by competing night-time background elements at Speedway Blvd/Rook Ave) is supported by a verbatim quote in EV-US-001 tied to the recorded case-study issue.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no compliance claim mixed in and normative_basis_note appropriately null.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Retroreflective border on the signal backplate is a specific, location-tied, viable FHWA-recognized conspicuity countermeasure actionable at final design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed road users if drivers misread or detect the beacon late, pairing driver conspicuity with VRU protection.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance interval adequacy for slower walkers at high-collision-frequency HAWK sites is a genuine, scheme-relevant safety issue squarely in scope for a final-design-stage signal timing review.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is backed by a verbatim quoted excerpt from EV-US-016 ('may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') matching the recorded FHWA case study issue for these exact sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern rather than a compliance question; verification of assumed walking speeds is framed as a safety check consistent with FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: reprogramme clearance intervals at all six named sites using a reduced assumed walking speed, a standard viable MUTCD-consistent remedy; not a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Elderly pedestrians are explicitly named as affected road users and are the explicit focus of both the scenario and the recommended timing change.
